story: After a creator deity formed the first humans, dust from his body became a hero and his twin brother, opposite in nature. The creator gave the hero power to shape a good world, while the twin brother sought only evil. The hero learned that hunters who killed too much would ruin the world he wished to preserve, so he sought out an old grandmother animal spirit, who wove her own body hair into a magical bag. The hero had hidden all the game animals in a river, boasting that people would never need to hunt again, but the grandmother scolded him, saying humans needed hunting to stay strong, so he released the animals. Later, the hero captured a great bird resting on a mountain peak whose wingbeats caused storms; he bound its wings until the air grew too still and hot to breathe, then loosened them just enough to allow bearable weather. In another account, the hero lay motionless for 365 days facing the rising sun, arms outstretched; afterward an old woman was born from dew on stone, a young man from sea foam, and a woman, mother of a people, from plants of the earth. The hero was said to have shaped valleys and other landforms, turned his evil twin to stone, and, as a giant beaver, slapped his tail to raise five islands from the sea. He painted the world's colors, dipping his brush to create his favorite island. He also slew a monstrous frog that had swallowed all the water, releasing rivers and lakes, and gave people earthenware, knowledge of good and evil, fire, tobacco, fishing nets, and canoes.
